questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The FIFA World Cup held in 2026 was won by:
questions.explanation: Spain won the 2026 FIFA World Cup, beating Argentina 1-0 after extra time in the final. 'Argentina' is wrong because Argentina were the beaten finalists, having won the previous edition in 2022. 'France' is wrong because France were the champions of 2018 and the runners-up of 2022 but did not win in 2026. 'Brazil' is wrong because Brazil's last title came in 2002, and although they remain the most successful side in the tournament's history they were not the 2026 winners.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the FIFA World Cup 2026:

(i) The final was decided after extra time by a single goal.
(ii) The tournament was jointly hosted by the United States, Canada and Mexico.
(iii) The winning country thereby became the first to hold the men's and women's World Cup titles at the same time.
(iv) The tournament was won by the same country that had won the previous edition.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct, the match being settled 1-0 in extra time. Statement (ii) is correct, the 2026 edition being the first shared by three host nations. Statement (iii) is correct, Spain having also held the women's title won in 2023. Statement (iv) is incorrect because the previous edition, in 2022, was won by ARGENTINA, and Argentina were the side Spain defeated in the 2026 final. Every option containing (iv) — the first, second and third — is therefore wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: As of July 2026, the Chief Minister of the Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir was:
questions.explanation: Omar Abdullah of the National Conference held office as Chief Minister of the Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir during 2026. 'Mehbooba Mufti' is wrong because she is the president of the Peoples Democratic Party and served as Chief Minister of the erstwhile state in an earlier period. 'Ghulam Nabi Azad' is wrong because he too headed the state government at an earlier time and later founded a separate party. 'Farooq Abdullah' is wrong because, although he has been Chief Minister in the past and leads the National Conference, the office in 2026 was held by his son.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the persons in Column I with the offices they held during 2026 in Column II:

Column I:
(a) Omar Abdullah
(b) Manoj Sinha
(c) Ashwini Vaishnaw
(d) Shashi Tharoor

Column II:
(i) Union Minister for Railways
(ii) Chief Minister of Jammu & Kashmir
(iii) Chairman of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on External Affairs
(iv) Lieutenant Governor of Jammu & Kashmir

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Omar Abdullah was Chief Minister of the Union Territory, Manoj Sinha its Lieutenant Governor, Ashwini Vaishnaw the Union Railways Minister, and Shashi Tharoor chaired the Parliamentary Standing Committee on External Affairs which met the Chief Minister in June 2026. The first option is wrong because it swaps the Chief Minister and the Lieutenant Governor. The second option is wrong because it makes a Union Minister the committee chairman and a Member of Parliament the Railways Minister. The fourth option is wrong because it assigns the Lieutenant Governor's office to a Union Minister.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Winter Olympic Games of February 2026 were hosted by:
questions.explanation: The 2026 Winter Games were held jointly at Milan and Cortina d'Ampezzo in Italy from 6 to 22 February 2026. 'Beijing in China' is wrong because Beijing hosted the preceding Winter Games in 2022, becoming the first city to host both a summer and a winter edition. 'Pyeongchang in South Korea' is wrong because it hosted the 2018 Winter Games. 'Sochi in Russia' is wrong because it hosted the Winter Games of 2014.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): After the 2026 final, Spain became the first country to hold the men's and the women's football World Cup titles simultaneously.
Reason (R): Spain had won the women's World Cup in 2023 and went on to win the men's title in 2026.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Both statements are true and (R) is exactly why (A) holds: holding both trophies at once requires winning the women's title and then the men's while the former is still current, which is precisely the sequence Spain completed in 2023 and 2026. The second option is wrong because the two victories together constitute the achievement rather than being an unrelated fact. The third option is wrong because the dates of the two Spanish triumphs are a matter of record. The fourth option is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are correct about the G20 in 2026?

(i) The presidency for the year was held by the United States.
(ii) The Leaders' Summit was scheduled to be held at Miami in December.
(iii) The G20 maintains a permanent secretariat which organises each summit.
(iv) A meeting of G20 Foreign Ministers was scheduled at Atlanta.

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Items (i), (ii) and (iv) are all correct: the United States held the 2026 presidency, the Leaders' Summit was set for Miami in December, and a Foreign Ministers' meeting was scheduled at Atlanta. Item (iii) is the exception, because the G20 has NO permanent secretariat; the presidency rotates annually and the country holding it makes the arrangements for that year. Hence the first option is wrong (it includes the secretariat claim and omits the Atlanta meeting), the second is wrong (it includes it and omits the presidency), and the third is wrong (it includes it and omits the Miami summit).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Vande Bharat Express introduced between Jammu and Srinagar in 2026 was significant chiefly because it:
options: provided the first direct rail link between the two capitals of Jammu & Kashmir
was the first train in India to be operated entirely on solar power
was the first Vande Bharat service to run anywhere in northern India
replaced the entire road transport service between the two cities
questions.correctAnswer: provided the first direct rail link between the two capitals of Jammu & Kashmir
questions.explanation: The service, flagged off by the Railways Minister, established the first direct rail connection between Jammu and Srinagar, the twin capitals of the Union Territory, covering the distance in about four hours and fifty minutes over the Udhampur-Srinagar-Baramulla corridor. 'Operated entirely on solar power' is wrong because the train draws power from the overhead electric traction system. 'The first Vande Bharat service in northern India' is wrong because such services had been running on several northern routes for years before this. 'Replaced the entire road transport service' is wrong because the national highway continues to carry heavy traffic.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The following details were recorded of the FIFA World Cup 2026 final:

Result: Spain 1, Argentina 0, decided in extra time
Shots attempted: Spain 20, Argentina 3
Argentina played the whole of extra time with ten men after a second yellow card
Scorer of the winning goal: Ferran Torres, who was named man of the match

Which of the following conclusions is correct?
options: Argentina attempted more shots than Spain but failed to convert any of them
The match was decided within the regulation ninety minutes of play
Spain attempted almost seven times as many shots as Argentina
Both sides finished the match with a full complement of eleven players
questions.correctAnswer: Spain attempted almost seven times as many shots as Argentina
questions.explanation: Spain's 20 attempts against Argentina's 3 gives a ratio of about 6.7 to one, so 'almost seven times as many' is an accurate reading of the data. The first option is wrong because it reverses the figures, Spain being the side that attempted far more shots. The second option is wrong because the data expressly state that the result was decided in extra time. The fourth option is wrong because Argentina were reduced to ten men after a second yellow card and played the whole of extra time a player short.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about events in Jammu & Kashmir in July 2026:

(i) The Amarnath Yatra was temporarily suspended following a forecast of widespread rainfall.
(ii) Flash floods and landslides caused loss of life in several districts.
(iii) The pilgrimages to Mata Vaishno Devi and Shiv Khori continued uninterrupted throughout.
(iv) The Lieutenant Governor reviewed the situation and directed that rescue operations be intensified.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements (i), (ii) and (iv) correctly describe the July 2026 spell of heavy weather: the yatra was halted after the meteorological warning, flash floods and landslides claimed lives, and the Lieutenant Governor assessed the position and ordered rescue work to be stepped up. Statement (iii) is incorrect because the pilgrimages to Mata Vaishno Devi and Shiv Khori were suspended as well, along with the Amarnath Yatra. Every option containing (iii) — the first, third and fourth — is therefore wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Nobel Peace Prize for 2025 was awarded to:
questions.explanation: The 2025 Nobel Peace Prize was conferred on María Corina Machado, the Venezuelan opposition leader. 'Nihon Hidankyo of Japan' is wrong because that organisation of atomic bomb survivors received the prize in 2024. 'Narges Mohammadi of Iran' is wrong because she was honoured in 2023. 'The World Food Programme' is wrong because that United Nations agency received the prize in 2020; all three are genuine recent laureates, which is what makes them close distractors.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the Nobel Prize categories for 2025 in Column I with the laureates in Column II:

Column I:
(a) Peace
(b) Literature
(c) Physics
(d) Economic Sciences

Column II:
(i) László Krasznahorkai
(ii) María Corina Machado
(iii) Joel Mokyr, Philippe Aghion and Peter Howitt
(iv) John Clarke, Michel Devoret and John Martinis

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: The 2025 Peace Prize went to María Corina Machado, the Literature Prize to the Hungarian writer László Krasznahorkai, the Physics Prize jointly to Clarke, Devoret and Martinis for work on quantum effects in electric circuits, and the Economics Prize to Mokyr, Aghion and Howitt for explaining innovation-driven growth. The second option is wrong because it swaps the peace and literature laureates. The third option is wrong because it interchanges the physics and economics teams. The fourth option is wrong because it makes a team of physicists the literature laureate and a novelist the physics laureate.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The G20 Leaders' Summit of 2026 was scheduled to be held in which city?
questions.explanation: With the United States holding the presidency for the year, the 2026 G20 Leaders' Summit was scheduled for Miami in Florida in December. 'Johannesburg' is wrong because South Africa held the presidency in the preceding cycle and hosted its summit there. 'Rio de Janeiro' is wrong because Brazil hosted the summit of 2024 in that city. 'New Delhi' is wrong because India hosted the G20 summit in 2023, though it was to host the BRICS leaders in 2026.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Brazil's medal at the 2026 Winter Olympic Games was a landmark in the history of those Games.
Reason (R): Brazil is a member of the BRICS grouping along with India, Russia and China.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but (R) is irrelevant to (A). The medal was a landmark because it was Brazil's first ever at a Winter Olympics and made it the first tropical, Latin American and South American committee to win one; its membership of an economic and political grouping has no bearing on that sporting first. The first option is wrong because it offers a diplomatic fact as the reason for a sporting achievement. The third option is wrong because Brazil is indeed a BRICS member, and the fourth is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: As of July 2026, the Lieutenant Governor of the Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir was:
questions.explanation: Manoj Sinha was serving as Lieutenant Governor of Jammu & Kashmir through 2026, chairing security reviews and addressing public functions such as the state-level job fair at Srinagar. 'G.C. Murmu' is wrong because he was the first Lieutenant Governor of the Union Territory and later became Comptroller and Auditor General of India. 'Satya Pal Malik' is wrong because he was Governor of the erstwhile state before its reorganisation. 'R.K. Mathur' is wrong because he served as Lieutenant Governor of Ladakh, a separate Union Territory.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are pilgrimages that were suspended in Jammu & Kashmir in July 2026 on account of heavy rainfall?

(i) The Amarnath Yatra
(ii) The pilgrimage to Mata Vaishno Devi
(iii) The Kailash Mansarovar Yatra
(iv) The pilgrimage to Shiv Khori

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: The Amarnath Yatra in the Kashmir valley and the pilgrimages to Mata Vaishno Devi and Shiv Khori in the Jammu region were all suspended after the meteorological department forecast widespread rain. The Kailash Mansarovar Yatra is the exception: it proceeds through Uttarakhand or Sikkim into Tibet and lies wholly outside Jammu & Kashmir, so it could not have been affected by this order. Hence the first option is wrong (it includes that yatra and omits Shiv Khori), the second is wrong (it includes it and omits Amarnath), and the third is wrong (it includes it and omits Vaishno Devi).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit of 2026, which the Indian Prime Minister was to attend, was held at:
questions.explanation: The 2026 SCO summit was held at Bishkek, the capital of Kyrgyzstan. 'Astana' is wrong because the Kazakh capital hosted an earlier SCO summit and is a plausible confusion among Central Asian venues. 'Samarkand' is wrong because the Uzbek city hosted the summit of 2022. 'Tashkent' is wrong because, although Uzbekistan's capital has hosted SCO meetings in the past, the 2026 gathering was in Kyrgyzstan.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Nobel Prizes for 2025:

(i) The Chemistry Prize recognised work on metal-organic frameworks.
(ii) The Physics Prize recognised work on quantum behaviour in superconducting electric circuits.
(iii) The Literature Prize was awarded to an Indian novelist.
(iv) The Prize in Economic Sciences recognised work explaining how innovation drives growth.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct, the chemistry award recognising porous frameworks able to harvest water from dry air and capture carbon dioxide. Statement (ii) is correct, the physics award concerning tunnelling and energy quantisation in superconducting circuits. Statement (iv) correctly describes the economics award. Statement (iii) is incorrect because the 2025 Literature Prize went to the Hungarian writer László Krasznahorkai; the only Indian to have won the Literature Prize remains Rabindranath Tagore in 1913. Every option containing (iii) — the first, second and fourth — is therefore wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Amarnath Yatra was temporarily suspended in July 2026 primarily because:
options: the shrine board had exhausted its annual quota of registrations
the India Meteorological Department forecast widespread heavy rainfall
the Union Territory was holding elections to the Legislative Assembly
the cave shrine was closed for structural repairs
questions.correctAnswer: the India Meteorological Department forecast widespread heavy rainfall
questions.explanation: The authorities halted the yatra as a precaution after the meteorological department warned of widespread rain across the Union Territory, and flash floods and landslides did in fact follow. 'Exhausted its annual quota of registrations' is wrong because the suspension was a weather measure and registration limits do not cause a mid-yatra halt. 'Holding elections to the Legislative Assembly' is wrong because no such polls were the cause, an elected government already being in office. 'Closed for structural repairs' is wrong because the shrine is a natural cave and no repair closure was reported.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: In 2026 India was to host the summit of the BRICS grouping in the city of __________.
questions.explanation: India was to welcome the BRICS leaders at New Delhi in 2026, as part of a period of summit diplomacy that also took the Prime Minister to Bishkek for the SCO meeting. 'Mumbai' and 'Bengaluru' are wrong because, although both have hosted large international meetings including G20 working sessions, the BRICS leaders' summit was set for the national capital. 'Goa' is wrong because Goa hosted the BRICS summit of 2016, which makes it a plausible but dated choice.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Vande Bharat train introduced on the Jammu-Srinagar route was built to a specification different from that of Vande Bharat trains running on the plains.
Reason (R): The railway line between Jammu and Srinagar runs entirely at sea level and passes through no tunnels.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct
questions.explanation: (A) is correct: the rake was given an all-weather design, reported as able to operate at about minus twenty degrees Celsius, with heating arrangements to stop water and braking systems from freezing. (R) is wrong on both counts, because the Udhampur-Srinagar-Baramulla line climbs through high mountainous country far above sea level and is carried through a long series of tunnels and bridges, including the Chenab bridge; indeed it is that terrain and its severe winters that make the special specification necessary. The first and second options are wrong because both require (R) to be correct, and the fourth is wrong because (A) is accurate.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The final of the FIFA World Cup 2026 was played at a stadium in:
options: the New York and New Jersey area
questions.correctAnswer: the New York and New Jersey area
questions.explanation: The final was staged at the New York New Jersey stadium, one of the principal venues of the tournament in the United States. 'Mexico City' is wrong because, although Mexico co-hosted and its Azteca stadium had staged two earlier World Cup finals, the 2026 decider was not held there. 'Toronto' is wrong because the Canadian venues hosted only earlier-round matches. 'Los Angeles' is wrong because it too was a host city but not the venue of the final.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The following facts were recorded about the Winter Olympic Games of 2026:

Dates: 6 to 22 February 2026
Number of countries winning at least one medal: 29
Total medals awarded across all disciplines: 346
Brazil won its first ever Winter Olympic medal, which was a gold

Which of the following conclusions is correct?
options: The Games awarded fewer than 300 medals in all
Brazil had previously won several Winter Olympic medals
On average, the medal-winning countries took more than ten medals each
The Games were held over a period of more than five weeks
questions.correctAnswer: On average, the medal-winning countries took more than ten medals each
questions.explanation: Dividing 346 medals among 29 medal-winning countries gives an average of about 11.9, which is indeed more than ten. The first option is wrong because 346 is well above 300. The second option is wrong because the data state that this was Brazil's FIRST ever Winter Olympic medal. The fourth option is wrong because 6 to 22 February is a span of about two and a half weeks, not more than five.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the international gatherings of 2026 in Column I with their venues in Column II:

Column I:
(a) G20 Leaders' Summit
(b) Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Summit
(c) BRICS Summit
(d) Winter Olympic Games

Column II:
(i) Bishkek
(ii) New Delhi
(iii) Miami
(iv) Milano Cortina d'Ampezzo

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: The G20 Leaders' Summit was set for Miami under the American presidency, the SCO summit was held at Bishkek in Kyrgyzstan, India was to host the BRICS leaders at New Delhi, and the Winter Games were staged at Milan and Cortina d'Ampezzo. The first option is wrong because it swaps the G20 and SCO venues. The third option is wrong because it interchanges the SCO and BRICS venues. The fourth option is wrong because it makes an Italian ski resort the site of a BRICS summit and New Delhi the site of the Winter Olympics.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the G20:

(i) Its presidency rotates annually among the member countries.
(ii) It holds annual summits attended by heads of state or government.
(iii) It also holds meetings of finance ministers and central bank governors.
(iv) India held the G20 presidency in 2026 and hosted the Leaders' Summit that year.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements (i), (ii) and (iii) correctly describe how the G20 works: an annually rotating presidency, a yearly leaders' summit, and parallel tracks of finance ministers and central bank governors. Statement (iv) is incorrect because the presidency in 2026 belonged to the UNITED STATES, which scheduled the summit at Miami; India's G20 presidency and New Delhi summit had taken place in 2023. Every option containing (iv) — the first, second and third — is therefore wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The winning goal in the FIFA World Cup 2026 final was scored by:
questions.explanation: Ferran Torres scored the only goal of the final in extra time and was named man of the match. 'Lionel Messi' is wrong because he was playing for the defeated Argentine side. 'Nico Williams' is wrong because, although he was involved in the move, he provided the assist rather than the finish. 'Lamine Yamal' is wrong because, although he was a prominent member of the Spanish side, the decisive goal was not his.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are correct about international sport in 2026?

(i) The FIFA World Cup was co-hosted by three countries.
(ii) The Winter Olympic Games were held in Italy.
(iii) India won its first Winter Olympic medal at those Games.
(iv) Brazil won a gold medal at the Winter Olympic Games.

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: The World Cup was shared by the United States, Canada and Mexico, the Winter Games were held in Italy, and Brazil took a gold medal there. Item (iii) is the exception: India's two competitors finished 39th and 104th in their events and India has still never won a Winter Olympic medal. Hence the first option is wrong (it includes the Indian medal claim and omits Brazil), the second is wrong (it includes it and omits the three co-hosts), and the fourth is wrong (it includes it and omits Italy as host).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: In July 2026 the Chief Minister of Jammu & Kashmir publicly contested the claim of a Union Minister concerning:
options: an examination paper leak in the Union Territory
the transfer of the Union Territory's police force
the revision of the electoral rolls
questions.correctAnswer: an examination paper leak in the Union Territory
questions.explanation: Omar Abdullah contested the Union Health Minister's statement on the recruitment paper leak in the Union Territory and asked the Centre to hold talks with the students protesting at Jantar Mantar in Delhi. 'The delimitation of Assembly constituencies' is wrong because the delimitation exercise had been completed earlier and was not the subject of this exchange. 'The transfer of the Union Territory's police force' is wrong because no such proposal was the matter in dispute. 'The revision of the electoral rolls' is wrong because the controversy concerned a recruitment examination and not the rolls.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the administration of Jammu & Kashmir in 2026:

(i) The Union Territory had an elected Chief Minister as well as a Lieutenant Governor.
(ii) The National Conference passed a resolution urging the restoration of full statehood.
(iii) The Chief Minister held that the decision on statehood rested with the Prime Minister and the Home Minister.
(iv) Full statehood had already been restored to Jammu & Kashmir during 2026.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct: an elected government under Omar Abdullah functioned alongside Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha, his party adopted a resolution demanding statehood, and he stated that the decision lay with the Prime Minister and the Home Minister. Statement (iv) is incorrect because statehood had NOT been restored; the continuing demand for it is precisely what the resolution and the protests of July 2026 were about. Every option containing (iv) — the first, second and third — is therefore wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Parliamentary Standing Committee that met the Chief Minister of Jammu & Kashmir in June 2026 was headed by:
questions.explanation: The Parliamentary Standing Committee on External Affairs, headed by Shashi Tharoor, met Omar Abdullah, who called for sustained engagement in understanding the aspirations of the people of the Union Territory. 'P. Chidambaram' is wrong because, although a senior parliamentarian and former Union Minister, he did not head this committee. 'Jairam Ramesh' is wrong for the same reason, his parliamentary work having lain with other committees. 'Anurag Thakur' is wrong because, although he has chaired a parliamentary committee, the external affairs committee in this instance was led by Shashi Tharoor.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the developments in Jammu & Kashmir during 2026 in Column I with the associated detail in Column II:

Column I:
(a) Suspension of the Amarnath Yatra
(b) The 77th State-Level Mega Job Fair
(c) The first direct Jammu-Srinagar train service
(d) The protest for restoration of statehood

Column II:
(i) Amar Singh College, Srinagar
(ii) Vande Bharat Express
(iii) Heavy rainfall and flash floods
(iv) Jantar Mantar, New Delhi

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: The yatra was halted because of heavy rain and flooding, the job fair was addressed by the Lieutenant Governor at Amar Singh College in Srinagar, the first direct link between the two capitals was a Vande Bharat service, and the statehood protest was held at Jantar Mantar in Delhi. The first option is wrong because it swaps the causes of the yatra suspension and the venue of the job fair. The second option is wrong because it makes a train service a protest site. The fourth option is wrong because it places the job fair in Delhi and the protest in a Srinagar college.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Nobel Prize in Literature for 2025 was awarded to:
questions.explanation: The 2025 Literature Prize went to the Hungarian writer László Krasznahorkai. 'Han Kang' is wrong because the South Korean novelist received the prize in 2024. 'Annie Ernaux' is wrong because the French writer was honoured in 2022. 'Abdulrazak Gurnah' is wrong because the Tanzanian-born novelist received it in 2021; all three are genuine recent laureates, which is what makes this a test of the precise year rather than of general familiarity.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): India held the presidency of the G20 during 2026 and hosted the Leaders' Summit at New Delhi that year.
Reason (R): The presidency of the G20 rotates annually among its member countries.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.explanation: (R) is correct: the presidency does pass from one member to another each year, which is why the venue of the summit changes. (A) is wrong on the year, because India's G20 presidency and the New Delhi Leaders' Summit belonged to 2023, whereas the 2026 presidency was held by the United States, which scheduled its summit at Miami. The first and second options are wrong because both require (A) to be correct, and the third is wrong because (R) is accurate.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are correct about rail connectivity in Jammu & Kashmir during 2025-26?

(i) Four pairs of new train services were introduced in the Jammu Division.
(ii) Two of those new pairs were Vande Bharat Express services.
(iii) The Jammu-Srinagar Vande Bharat covers the journey in under five hours.
(iv) The Jammu-Srinagar service was the first metro rail line in the Union Territory.

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Four pairs of new services were introduced in the Jammu Division during 2025-26, two of them Vande Bharat pairs, and the Jammu-Srinagar train covers the distance in about four hours and fifty minutes, which is under five hours. Item (iv) is the exception, because a Vande Bharat is a long-distance inter-city train on the national broad gauge network and has nothing to do with a metro rail system. Hence the first option is wrong (it includes the metro claim and omits the journey time), the second is wrong (it includes it and omits the four pairs), and the third is wrong (it includes it and omits the Vande Bharat pairs).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Winter Olympic Games of 2026 were held between:
questions.explanation: The 2026 Winter Games ran from 6 to 22 February, a little over a fortnight, which is the customary length of a Winter Olympics. '6 and 22 January' is wrong because the Games are not held in January, when many venues are still preparing. '1 and 17 March' is wrong because March is too late in the season for reliable snow at several venues. '20 February and 8 March' is wrong because that window corresponds more closely to the Paralympic Winter Games, which follow the Olympics.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the FIFA World Cup 2026 final:

(i) The goalkeeper of the losing side set a record for the number of saves in a World Cup final.
(ii) The winning goal was scored during the second period of extra time.
(iii) The losing side finished the match with eleven players on the field.
(iv) The player who scored the winning goal was named man of the match.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements (i), (ii) and (iv) are all correct: the Argentine goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez made a record number of saves in a final, Ferran Torres struck in the second period of extra time, and he was named man of the match. Statement (iii) is incorrect because Argentina were reduced to TEN men when Enzo Fernández received a second yellow card late in normal time, and they played the whole of extra time a player short. Every option containing (iii) — the first, second and fourth — is therefore wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The meeting of G20 Foreign Ministers scheduled for October 2026 was to be hosted in which city?
questions.explanation: The United States, holding the G20 presidency, scheduled the Foreign Ministers' meeting at Atlanta in Georgia for the end of October 2026. 'Washington' is wrong because, although the capital hosted early Sherpa and Finance Track meetings of the American presidency, the ministerial meeting was placed elsewhere. 'Chicago' is wrong because it was not among the announced venues. 'Miami' is wrong because Miami was the venue of the Leaders' Summit in December rather than of the Foreign Ministers' meeting.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: In July 2026 the Chief Minister of Jammu & Kashmir was stopped by the police while attempting to reach __________ in New Delhi to join a protest demanding the restoration of statehood.
questions.explanation: Jantar Mantar in New Delhi is the designated site for demonstrations near Parliament, and it was there that the protest for the restoration of statehood was being held when Omar Abdullah was stopped near the Parliament Police Station. 'India Gate' is wrong because it is a war memorial where demonstrations are not permitted. 'Rashtrapati Bhavan' is wrong because it is the President's residence and a high-security precinct. 'Vijay Chowk' is wrong because, although close to Parliament, it is not the recognised protest venue.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Nobel Prize in Physics for 2025 was awarded for work relating to:
options: quantum tunnelling and energy quantisation in electric circuits
the detection of gravitational waves from merging black holes
the development of high-resolution electron microscopy
the discovery of exoplanets orbiting distant stars
questions.correctAnswer: quantum tunnelling and energy quantisation in electric circuits
questions.explanation: John Clarke, Michel Devoret and John Martinis were honoured for experiments showing that billions of electrons in a superconducting circuit on a chip can collectively display quantum tunnelling and quantised energy levels, results that underpin much work on quantum computing. 'The detection of gravitational waves' is wrong because that was recognised by the 2017 prize. 'High-resolution electron microscopy' is wrong because microscopy advances have been recognised chiefly in chemistry. 'The discovery of exoplanets' is wrong because that was part of the 2019 physics award.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The number of countries that won at least one medal at the Winter Olympic Games of 2026 was:
questions.explanation: Twenty-nine countries finished the 2026 Winter Games with at least one medal, out of a total of 346 medals awarded across all disciplines, and Brazil was among those entering the list for the first time. '19' and '24' are wrong because both understate the spread of medals, which has widened as more nations invest in winter sport. '35' is wrong because it overstates it; the number of medal-winning countries at a Winter Games remains far smaller than at a Summer Games.
